name: Palingenetic ultranationalism
summary: Roger Griffin's term for what he takes to be the minimum of generic fascism: an ultranationalism built on the myth that a decadent nation will be reborn through a revolution that sweeps away the liberal, socialist and conservative old order. It mobilizes the people as a unified mass under a new elite and sometimes a heroic leader, treats violence as part of renewal, and is anti-liberal, anti-Marxist and anti-conservative. Economics, leadership forms and racial doctrine vary by movement and are not part of the core.
scope: Griffin's 'fascist minimum' (The Nature of Fascism, 1991) as the core of interwar generic fascism, filled in where the core is silent from Mussolini and Gentile's Doctrine of Fascism (1932) and Payne and Paxton's generic descriptions as summarized on Wikipedia. Economic, institutional and racial positions Griffin treats as contingent are answered at low confidence or neutral. Excludes postwar neo-fascism and non-fascist authoritarian nationalism (para-fascism).

sources.author: Library of Social Science

sources.title: Fascism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Generic features per Griffin, Payne and Paxton: dirigisme, autarky, expansion, militarism, gender style, one-party rule.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage-floor doctrine in the core; fascist regimes fixed wages by state decree within corporatist bodies, so a legislated substantial rise is not an adherent priority.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fascist economics is dirigiste, with the state directing activity toward national goals, and the Doctrine rejects economic liberalism outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Griffin treats economic form as contingent; interwar regimes mostly kept private firms under state direction rather than nationalizing utilities, so mild disagreement.

unions-good.rationale: The Doctrine admits union interests only inside the state's corporative system and rejects class struggle, so autonomous unions are not endorsed as good.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates the individual to the state, and property was held to serve the nation, so property is not an overriding right.

cut-welfare.rationale: Nothing in the core on welfare cuts; regimes built welfare organizations for nation members, which points mildly against cutting.

worker-ownership.rationale: Fascism rejects class-based ownership claims and keeps workers inside state-coordinated guilds rather than owning firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not in Griffin's core; radical anti-liberal movements put security of the national community above privacy, an inference from the Doctrine's primacy of the state.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Fascism rejects liberal speech norms but would not accept limits protecting groups it targets; no direct statement in the sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Griffin treats the leader cult as contingent, but the myth typically has one hero battling the old system with followers' infinite faith, and the Doctrine prizes authority. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

state-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine says outside the state no human or spiritual values exist; the nation's rebirth is pursued through state power.

empower-police-military.rationale: Militarism and paramilitary organization characterize fascism and the Doctrine glorifies the state as power that makes its will felt.

decide-locally.rationale: The Doctrine's all-embracing state and ultranationalist unity favour centralization over local decision-making.

traditional-family.rationale: Fascist movements promote family as the base of national renewal, though Griffin's minimum does not require it and some strands stressed modern youth.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Rebirth myths cast decadence as the enemy, and fascist regimes upheld traditional gender and family norms.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not in the core; fascist regimes banned or restricted abortion to serve national population goals, but this is a regime practice, not core doctrine.

more-religion-public.rationale: Griffin calls fascism a secular political religion built on national myth; most fascists sought synthesis with traditional religion, so adherents split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Fascist style promotes masculinity and fixed roles; a social-construct view conflicts with the organic nation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ultranationalism and the rebirth of the national community make preserving and renewing national culture central.

gradual-change.rationale: Griffin stresses fascism is anti-conservative and revolutionary: the new order needs a break, not gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigrants are among the Others fascism may demonize as threats to the nation, though the minimum itself does not specify numbers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Doctrine has nothing to do with universal embraces and demands that the nation stand on its own power; ultranationalism opposes supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: Dirigiste fascism pursued autarky and national self-sufficiency, so free trade is rejected.

nation-first.rationale: Ultranationalism is half of Griffin's fascist minimum: the nation's interests override global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The Doctrine justifies force for national power and conquest, not human rights; universalist rationales are rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Ultranationalism and a bounded organic nation are incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Fascist regimes pursued growth and power; no documented environmental limits position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Fascism embraces modernity when compatible with rebirth but also spiritualist reaction against positivism; adherents are split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Griffin's core is a revolutionary myth where destruction of the decadent order precedes national rebirth.

experts-over-public.rationale: Fascism distrusts both mass numbers and technocratic liberal elites, wanting a new elite defined by commitment to the national vision.

central-planning.rationale: Fascist economies were dirigiste with private ownership retained, not centrally planned; the Doctrine rejects socialist economic determinism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Griffin keeps economics outside the core; fascism rejects the class-based ownership premise behind the statement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not in the core; national movements generally protected family continuity.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Autarky and national self-sufficiency are standard dirigiste fascist aims, though Griffin treats economic form as contingent.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Fascism favours a dirigiste economy where the state strongly directs activity toward national goals.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not in the core; some fascists idealized small owners and peasants while regimes accommodated large firms.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Doctrine rejects historic materialism and the Marxist programme, and work is valued as an ethical activity.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-directed national economy has no place for abolishing central monetary institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporative guilds were fascism's standard arrangement of class relations (Doctrine), though Griffin deems corporatism contingent.

one-party-rule.rationale: Fascists often advocate a totalitarian one-party state, but Griffin says specific institutional forms are not part of the minimum. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Doctrine says republics and monarchies can both be reactionary or daring, so it is indifferent; strands differ.

democracy-best.rationale: The Doctrine denies the right of numbers to govern through periodic consultation; Griffin says fascism is hostile to liberal democratic institutions.

direct-votes.rationale: Populist rhetoric appeals to the whole people, but the Doctrine rejects counting majorities; plebiscitary acclaim is not a deliberative direct vote.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power rest on class politics, which fascism denies and subordinates to the national state.

right-to-secede.rationale: An organic, unified ultranationalist state cannot grant regions the right to leave.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Doctrine asserts the beneficial inequality of men and Griffin describes a vanguard elite chosen for commitment to the national vision.

political-violence-never.rationale: Violence is linked to the renewal myth (destruction and creation as one process), and the Doctrine glorifies struggle.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Doctrine says war alone raises human energies to their maximum tension and ennobles peoples.

separate-church-state.rationale: Fascists treated religion as a national resource and the Doctrine claims to be a religious conception; strands differ on formal separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Griffin calls fascism a secular myth; the state, not scripture, is the source of values in the Doctrine.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Doctrine's state is all-embracing and monopolises power; private provision is incompatible.

military-superiority.rationale: The Doctrine says the state is power felt beyond its frontiers, and fascism glorifies militarized national greatness.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Griffin says ultranationalism covers many forms of ethnocentrism, but the Doctrine defines the nation as a historical people rather than a race, so some variance.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Doctrine denies historic materialism and the irreparable character of class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Doctrine asserts the fertile and beneficent inequality of men and rejects leveling.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Ultranationalism rejects the claims of sub-national peoples against the unitary state and its territory.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Fascist imperial ambition and national pride treat colonial rule as national greatness, not debt.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Doctrine rejects selfish individualism in favour of duty, sacrifice and the nation's good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Doctrine says life means duty and accepts the individual only as his interests coincide with the state's.

limit-population.rationale: Regeneration of the nation is tied to national vitality and expansion, which regimes pursued through pronatalism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fascism claims modernity where compatible with rebirth and rejects anti-modern withdrawal.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Both embrace of modern power and spiritualist reaction against positivism appear; adherents split.

human-enhancement.rationale: No stated position; the new-man ideal is moral and national rather than technological.

restore-past-order.rationale: Griffin: rebirth is a new order, not a return to the past, although a golden age may serve as guide.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Doctrine claims action preceded doctrine, yet movements are driven by a mythic core; adherents split.

direct-action.rationale: The Doctrine says fascism was born of action, and paramilitary action has been a common method.

means-match-ends.rationale: Paxton describes redemptive violence without ethical or legal restraints, so means are not bound to match ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rebirth within a modern society is the aim, not a primitive withdrawal.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The Doctrine values work and corporative coordination of economic functions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the economic interpretation of felicity as a socialist entitlement.

production-for-use.rationale: Production is aimed at national power and self-sufficiency rather than a use-value doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects Marxist exploitation theory and class conflict, treating labor and capital as united in the state.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Griffin states socialism was the phoenix of the old order, not the nation, and the Doctrine rejects class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization is a socialist programme opposed by fascism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Fascism treats war as ennobling and inevitable, not a product of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Doctrine's state is entitled to the individual's service and resources.

harm-principle.rationale: The Doctrine opposes liberal individualism and puts the state above individual liberty.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Doctrine says the individual is accepted only in so far as interests coincide with the state's.

conscription.rationale: The Doctrine's duty ethic and militarized nation support compulsory service; no explicit statement in Griffin.

state-as-business.rationale: The Doctrine calls the state a spiritual and ethical entity, not a business.

media-academia-power.rationale: Fascists attacked liberal elites but the sources do not document this specific claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Nazi variant was biological, but the generic minimum and the Italian Doctrine define the nation as a people rather than a race.

organic-representation.rationale: The Doctrine represents people through classes and guilds inside the state rather than counted individuals.

total-state.rationale: The Doctrine says the fascist state is all-embracing and nothing human or spiritual exists outside it.

national-rebirth.rationale: National rebirth from decadence is the definitional core of palingenetic ultranationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Payne's fascist goals include expansion into an empire, and the Doctrine ties national vitality to power beyond frontiers.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The leader cult is contingent in Griffin, and loyalty is meant to be to the nation's vision.

universal-morality.rationale: The Doctrine rejects universal embraces and abstractions; morality is national.

single-common-good.rationale: Fascism assumes a unified national interest in which classes and individuals merge.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democratic premises and class representation within firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is a state tool to shape the new national citizen, per the Doctrine.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Dirigiste regimes used state spending for national aims; no stated fiscal doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Doctrine is definitely and absolutely opposed to liberalism in the political and economic sphere.

force-without-un.rationale: The Doctrine denies perpetual peace and accepts force as proof of national rights.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Doctrine mocks positivism and founds action on myth and will; Griffin treats fascism as political religion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Regimes provided benefits to members of the national community; documented by practice rather than doctrine.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Doctrine says the state unites classes into one economic and ethical reality.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Ultranationalism and the golden-age strand value heritage, though a new order replaces much of the old.

workers-nation.rationale: Fascist national syndicalism wanted workers integrated into the nation, but Griffin treats this as contingent.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Fascist style promotes masculinity and youth, with distinct roles typical.

ban-interest.rationale: The sources are silent on interest bans; fascist regimes worked with banks and private credit, so mildly against.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Ethnocentrism varies across strands; the Italian doctrine defined the nation otherwise than by race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Doctrine denies the state is an instrument of class and treats it as the nation's will.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Ethnocentric ultranationalism may reject assimilation or demand it; strands differ.

elite-replacement.rationale: Griffin: fascism promises youth, heroism and national greatness in place of gerontocracy, mediocrity and weakness, replacing old elites.

proportional-representation.rationale: Hostile to parliamentary party competition; the Doctrine rejects counting numbers.

national-mission.rationale: Fascist ultranationalism often casts the nation as having a historic mission; the Doctrine speaks of the nation's will to power and a universal character of its decisions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Fascist style promotes masculinity and fixed roles; structural patriarchy critique is rejected.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The populist myth casts existing elites as decadent and alien to the common man.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Doctrine says state functions cannot be limited to order and peace as liberal doctrine had it.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Applies to racist variants but not to the generic core or the Italian Doctrine's definition of the nation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Doctrine asserts the beneficial inequality of men and Griffin calls the nation anti-egalitarian.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonial settlement was approved by fascists; the statement is a critique they reject.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Fascists synthesized with traditional religions; no statement about conversion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Doctrine values religion and education as shaped by the state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Doctrine rejects sovereignty of numbers and treats authority as emanating from the state.

population-transfer.rationale: Cleansing of non-members appears in some variants but not in the core.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and conquest as nobility-conferring.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Struggle among nations is celebrated, but the Doctrine rejects liberal economic competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Liberty is only the state's and the individual's within the state, per the Doctrine.

separated-powers.rationale: The Doctrine's all-embracing state rejects checks; Griffin says fascism is anti-parliamentary.

vanguard-party.rationale: Griffin describes a vanguard elite of committed followers; the Doctrine's party shapes the state.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Fascism privileges the nation as a whole over any class priority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were suppressed in the corporative system to enforce class collaboration.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ultranationalism seeks a unified people; Others are cast as threats.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection by chance denies the elite principle of the new vanguard. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Paxton describes redemptive violence without ethical or legal restraints, and the Doctrine denies rights outside the state.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-directed economies fixed prices; not a doctrinal requirement.

party-controls-media.rationale: Totalitarian fascist regimes controlled media; contingent on regime form.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Doctrine's party is a political educator; fascist regimes balanced party and army differently.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Representation by class guilds under elite leadership, not worker-pay equivalence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Ultranationalism rejects pooling sovereignty and the Doctrine insists on national power.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Leader as military commander is typical of the style, but the Doctrine does not formalize it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Griffin's fascism is secular and the state rules, so clerical rule is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Fascist nationalism treats the nation's war effort as sacred, and defeatism as cowardice.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Leaders hold power without term limits; leader cult is contingent in Griffin.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall lets voters overturn leaders, which conflicts with the Doctrine's denial of the right of numbers to govern through periodic consultation.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Fascist states sought alliances for power; no principle against them.

people-in-arms.rationale: Mass mobilization and paramilitary organization are common in fascism.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Soil-based national romanticism existed in some variants; not core.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Irredentism and expanding the nation into its claimed whole are typical ultranationalist aims in the generic descriptions (s4), but Griffin's minimum does not include them, so this is an inference.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populism treats establishment elites as alien to the common man.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ultranationalism ranks the nation above others and denies universalist equality.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnocentric nation concept; the Doctrine itself says a people historically perpetuating itself.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Doctrine demands individuals fit state aims, and denies selfish individualism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not tie political independence to economic transformation as a doctrine; neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rejects parliamentary mechanics; a revolutionary leader or movement imposes the new order.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The state subordinates individual liberty to national goals including economic power.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nation-first ultranationalism rejects universal obligations toward other peoples, and the Doctrine says fascism will have nothing to do with universal embraces.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Plebiscitary acclaim of a leader is common, but the sources give no position on the formal election of a head of state, so neutral.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state directs the economy; independent monetary institutions conflict.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Doctrine makes economic activity serve the state, and property subordinate to national need.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Expansion of nation into empire is a fascist goal, so occupation is not treated as wrong.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Doctrine says outside the state no spiritual values exist; church serves national life.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Force for national unity follows from ultranationalism and the Doctrine's will to power.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The leader cult is contingent and the leader is revered as a mythic hero by followers.

character-from-environment.rationale: Italian doctrine stresses spiritual formation while Nazi variants stressed heredity, so adherents split; neutral.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The state's will is above liberal legal constraint in the Doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rejects mixed liberal constitutions in favour of authoritarian democracy.

leader-cult.rationale: Griffin makes the leader cult contingent, but the myth typically features infinite faith in a mythical hero.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources are silent; ultranationalist views differ by which nation's refugees are at issue, so neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ultranationalism often claims territory where kin live, though not defined in the minimum.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-national unions of kindred peoples appeared in some variants but are not part of the minimum, so neutral.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Unified nation with one culture rejects autonomy of sub-communities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Citizenship in the national community is central, so residence alone is insufficient.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Doctrine denies that economics suffice to explain history.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state directs the economy and may rescue national firms.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is standard in dirigiste fascism, though contingent per Griffin.

moral-incentives.rationale: Doctrine promotes duty, sacrifice and heroism without economic motive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Interwar fascist movements relied on paramilitary squads to create the revolutionary situation, as the Doctrine's punitive expeditions illustrate.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: New elites replace old ones, yet fascists allied with traditional elites.

patriotic-education.rationale: Doctrine gives high importance to education in shaping nation members.

delink-world-market.rationale: Autarky is a fascist goal yet the statement is a leftist formulation.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Doctrine grants rights only inside and through the state, so entrenched protections against it are rejected.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers emerge from vanguard and not from elections in the Doctrine's critique of numbers.

minority-veto.rationale: A veto for minorities contradicts the single national will that the Doctrine places above partial groups.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Griffin describes fascism as anti-parliamentary and the Doctrine rejects government by periodic consultation of numbers.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Doctrine demands active commitment and heroism; withdrawal is abdication.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Autarky and national self-sufficiency are standard aims of dirigiste fascism, which prefer self-reliance over foreign aid.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Antifascism is the direct negation of the fascist myth, which treated liberals and socialists as the decadent old order.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Griffin treats communism and fascism as different; fascists reject equation.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Doctrine defines the nation as a historically perpetuating people with its own spirit, implying institutions suited to it; medium.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Autarky and national self-sufficiency favour protecting national firms from foreign buyers.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegation with recall is a council-democratic device that the Doctrine's authoritarian state rejects.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Griffin describes fascism as anti-parliamentary, so budget control by parliament is rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine attacks the materialism and pursuit of pleasure of the nineteenth century and praises heroism without economic motive.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fascist regimes ran demographic campaigns to renew national vitality, in keeping with the rebirth myth.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Doctrine rejects both democracy and the possibility of perpetual peace, so this claim is rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Doctrine requires the individual to serve the state, so a denial of any duty to obey is rejected.

non-intervention.rationale: The Doctrine treats power beyond frontiers as proof of vitality, so strict non-intervention is rejected.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy beliefs appear in some variants, not in the generic core.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Doctrine says no individuals or groups, including associations and classes, exist outside the state.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Ultranationalism places national sovereignty above international obligation.

religious-nation.rationale: Griffin treats fascism as a secular myth of national rebirth, and most fascists sought a synthesis with traditional religion rather than a confessional nation, so mild disagreement.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nation-first ultranationalism rejects deference to another power, though tactical alliances occurred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A unitary national state and a single national interest argue against regions keeping revenue.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism is one of Payne's fascist negations, and Griffin treats socialism as a rival old order to be overcome.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Doctrine calls fascism a religious conception of life, and fascists did not call religion an illusion.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism appeared in some regimes but is not part of the minimum, so neutral.

treaties-binding.rationale: Doctrine views treaties as conditional on national will and power.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communes outside the state conflict with the Doctrine's all-embracing state.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Doctrine: opposed to both liberal economics and Marxism; third-way.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is a feature of postwar neo-fascism, not of the generic core, so adherents of the profile's scope are split; neutral.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Regimes differed on it and the generic core is silent, so neutral.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Hostile to parliamentary opposition per Griffin; suppression is a regime practice.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperial expansion for national benefit is among the fascist goals Payne lists.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the democratic premises of popular sovereignty by numbers.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An egalitarian critique that the anti-egalitarian nationalism of fascism rejects.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fascism claimed to be beyond left and right in some statements, but the sources do not give a settled position, so neutral.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Doctrine rejects Marxist historic materialism and treats work as the creative value of man.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from the nation and the state in the Doctrine, not from a divine grant.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Doctrine rejects liberal economics and welfare-capitalist compromise, favouring state direction instead.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and the armed nation, so abolishing armed forces is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: The Doctrine places the nation above class, so privileging the wealthy as such is not an adherent position.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Griffin treats economics as contingent; fascist regimes were dirigiste but left banking to the state and private owners, with no user-owned credit doctrine.

property-franchise.rationale: The core mobilizes the people as a unified mass, so a wealth test on voting is not an adherent aim, though fascism cared little for meaningful elections either.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Fascists attacked liberal freedoms as bourgeois fictions but suppressed independent press under state control; adherents' view of this claim is mixed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Griffin treats racial doctrine as contingent: Italian fascism was not initially racial while Nazism was, so adherents are split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religion and racial doctrine are not part of the core; some movements restricted mixed marriage on racial grounds and others did not.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Contingent on a movement's racial or religious doctrine, which Griffin excludes from the core; Nazi boycotts exist but Italian fascism's early phase had none.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Fascist movements varied from clerical allies to pagan or secular ones, and the core has no religious doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Griffin's core is silent; fascist doctrine subordinated individual liberty to the nation and did not frame wealth as a threat to liberty, though it attacked plutocracy.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism holds the state is spiritual and ethical and respected Catholicism as the Italian tradition; it did not promote atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies the authority of the state and its coercive order; abolishing police and prisons contradicts that.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Palingenetic ultranationalism rests on a single organic nation, so guaranteed shares for communities are rejected as division of the national community.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Griffin's core is silent; fascist regimes built state welfare organisations while also using party charity, so adherents did not agree.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the sovereignty of individual voters and liberal democracy as a 'rotting' form of rule.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Fascist regimes upheld patriarchal family order with the man as head, per the general descriptions in s4.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Interwar fascist movements and regimes ran uniformed youth organisations, but Griffin counts paramilitarism as contingent rather than core.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects pacifism and says war brings all human energy to its highest tension, so renouncing lethal force is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The rebirth myth presupposes a nation with a glorious past that fell into decadence, so continuity from antiquity is central; the Doctrine also invokes Roman heritage.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The cult of the fallen and sacralised sacrifice for the nation is a recurring feature of generic fascism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Doctrine describes fascism as a spiritual conception of life, and Griffin's rebirth myth is a quasi-religious renewal against decadence.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Doctrine holds that the state creates the nation and gives it will and life, so building the state comes first, not cultural renewal alone.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Racial and ethnic doctrine varies by movement and is contingent for Griffin, but ultranationalists commonly favoured the majority nation in economic life.

independent-unions.rationale: Fascist regimes dissolved independent unions and folded labour into state-run corporations under the Doctrine's 'everything within the state'.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The core is silent on utilities; fascist regimes mixed state ownership with private enterprise and adherents were not united.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Doctrine and Griffin's unified-nation myth reject decentralised assemblies; the state is a single will standing above all parts.

person-over-state.rationale: The Doctrine states that the individual exists only within the state and subordinate to it, and that fascism is against individualism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Doctrine calls fascism a spiritual conception of life, and Griffin's rebirth myth is a mythic and quasi-religious renewal; the state serves the spirit of the nation.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Fascist regimes were centralist and held all regional powers at the centre's pleasure, though self-government is not part of the core.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Griffin treats racial doctrine as contingent; Nazism was biologically racist while Italian Fascism initially was not, so adherents differ.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in the national or ethnic community is central to ultranationalism, though race as such varies by movement.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Doctrine says only war brings human energies to their highest tension and rejects perpetual peace; generic fascism includes expansion and militarism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Griffin's core centres on an organic national community reborn; language and history as its markers are common across movements but not part of the core.

communal-electorates.rationale: The core treats the nation as a unified mass under a new elite, and the Doctrine of Fascism rejects divided representation; separate communal electorates contradict it.

free-public-college.rationale: Griffin treats economics and social policy as contingent; fascist regimes varied.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Fascist movements assigned women distinct roles, but not the value of care and nonviolence in public life; the core is silent.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects pacifism and sees war as ennobling, and violence is part of the renewal myth.

capital-controls.rationale: Interwar fascist regimes used state control of finance and autarky, though Griffin treats economics as contingent.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Griffin counts paramilitarism as contingent; fascist movements used party militias before power and then centralised force in the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Doctrine holds that war alone brings human energy to its highest tension and that fascism rejects pacifism, so refusing orders is repudiated.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Fascist regimes replaced independent unions with state-run corporations, though Griffin treats economics as contingent.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Welfare for the nation's members varied, and Griffin's core is silent on tax credits.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Griffin's rebirth myth requires sweeping away the liberal, socialist and conservative order, though fascists took over the state and enlarged it rather than dissolving it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Fascism demands a unified national mass under one party and state, and the Doctrine rejects liberal pluralism.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Doctrine describes the nation as an ethical, spiritual entity that lives beyond individuals, and Griffin's core is ultranationalism built on its rebirth.

public-service-media.rationale: Fascist states controlled press and broadcasting as tools of national mobilisation under one-party rule, which is the opposite of independence from government.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Doctrine rejects class struggle and fascist regimes banned independent parties, so a separate workers' party is rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates liberty to the nation, but the environment was not a priority; no clear inference.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Fascist corporatism abolished free unions and bound workers into compulsory state-run syndicates, so voluntary membership is rejected.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects liberal democracy and electoral competition as decadent, and Griffin's core is anti-liberal.

women-suffrage.rationale: Interwar fascist movements generally cast women in domestic and maternal roles and did not support equal political rights, though suffrage was moot where elections were abolished.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects internationalism and perpetual peace and glorifies the nation's own power, so trial of leaders by courts above the nation is rejected.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Griffin treats religion as contingent; the Doctrine respects religion without scriptural literalism, and movements differed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Griffin defines the core as anti-Marxist and the Doctrine of Fascism rejects socialism, so defending a Marxist planned state is rejected.

national-church-status.rationale: Griffin treats religion as contingent; some movements favoured a national church and others were hostile or indifferent.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The core myth is of a unified national people reborn as one mass, and fascist states pursued centralised uniformity, so ethnic territorial autonomy is rejected.

simple-living.rationale: The Doctrine stresses duty and seriousness, but fascist regimes also pursued autarky and prosperity; the sources are split on this.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Griffin's core is an ultranationalism of national rebirth, and Gentile's Doctrine treats the nation as a spiritual unity tied to its land and past.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Fascist movements pursued irredentist claims for co-nationals outside their borders, as the general descriptions of fascism in s4 note.

self-ownership.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism holds that the individual exists only within the state and subordinates individual rights to it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Griffin treats economic policy as contingent and the sources describe no consumption-tax stance.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design varies by movement and is not part of the palingenetic core.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Griffin treats economic arrangements as contingent, and fascist regimes both favoured and constrained business.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Fascist movements differed, from the Lateran settlement in Italy to neo-pagan currents; the core does not settle it.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Griffin describes palingenetic ultranationalism as seeking a new modern order of national rebirth that draws on myth of the nation's past, combining both.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Griffin treats economics as contingent; fascist regimes were dirigiste and autarkic but never made this a core demand.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Griffin treats racial doctrine as varying between movements, so the core gives no answer.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Doctrine holds that nothing human or spiritual exists outside the state, which leaves no standard above positive law for citizens to appeal to.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Fascists claimed to unite nation and producers through class collaboration, but rejected the solidarity with workers abroad that the statement includes.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Fascist one-party states kept private enterprise under state direction and corporatist control (s4), which is close to this but not the same as communist leadership.

missingStatements.text: The state should aim to create a new kind of citizen through education and mass mobilization.
missingStatements.rationale: Griffin ties national rebirth to a new birth of the people under a vanguard and the Doctrine gives the state the task of educator and promoter of spiritual life; no existing statement captures this.

notes: Griffin's definition is a scholarly minimum, not a programme. Many economic, institutional and racial answers are borrowed from interwar practice and the Italian Doctrine and are low confidence; Nazi biological racism and postwar neo-fascism would answer differently. Critics argue the definition underplays violence and anti-Marxism.
